results.title: Scientific Data Analysis Pipelines and Reproducibility | by Altuna Akalin | TDS Archive | Medium
results.content: # Scientific Data Analysis Pipelines and Reproducibility. In addition, you need to know exact versions and configurations of the dependencies to have a shot at reproducing the data analysis pipeline. This will remain so even if we are promised to get a working pipeline that reproduces the authors version after we go through installation of each dependency diligently. ***Runtime environment reproducibility:*** The installed software should behave the same in every machine, in the sense that we need to install the very same software in every machine. Therefore, this software can behave differently even though same version is installed on two different machines because of dependency differences. If you can install the same exact software, built the same way with exactly the same dependencies down to the compiler, you have good chances at reproducing the runtime environment across different machines and therefore the analysis with the same input data. In practical terms, what many of us have in mind when we want to use a published data analysis tool is the following : 1) “can I install the published software at all and get similar results ? Or they should make sure when users install the pipeline they get identical versions of the dependencies. This means that if you can manage to install your pipeline and dependencies in this light-weight virtual machine, you can ship the container and be sure that anyone who uses that container will be able to reproduce your software environment. You can either build your pipeline as a bona fide software and package that using the package managers or provide list of packages from the package manager to be installed. If you can make sure the installed software is identical bit-by-bit on different systems, you can have runtime reproducibility and have the same results with same input data (minus the caveats mentioned in “*Runtime environment reproducibility*” subsection). For the reproducibility and robustness it provides, we opted to use Guix to manage dependencies of our pipelines. Making the data analysis pipelines reproducible should be the aim for the scientists if they want their tools or approach to be used by a wider audience.

results.title: How to Ensure Reproducibility in Data Analytics
results.content: Ensure reproducibility in data analytics by documenting every step of your analysis, including data preprocessing, transformations, and modeling. Ensuring reproducibility in data analytics hinges on code quality. To ensure transparency, accessibility, and reproducibility of data analytics, it is important to follow best practices such as literate programming tools to combine code, text, and output in a single document; notebooks and markdown formats to create interactive and dynamic documents; data visualization tools to create clear and informative charts and graphs; citation and referencing tools to acknowledge the sources and contributions of data and code; online platforms and repositories to publish and share data, code, and documents; as well as open and reproducible research standards and guidelines to report and present data analysis. This ensures not just code but the entire data analysis workflow is transparent, traceable, and consequently reproducible across different teams and projects. To ensure data analytics reproducibility in R, use version control, scripts, structured projects, package management, environment documentation, and code comments.

results.content: Reproducibility is the cornerstone of scientific integrity in statistical data science. Key components of reproducibility include data availability, code sharing, documentation, and version control. * Reproducibility forms the cornerstone of scientific integrity in Reproducible and Collaborative Statistical Data Science. ### Scientific method and reproducibility. * Promotes transparency in the research process, allowing scrutiny of methods and data. * Reproducibility in statistical data science relies on several interconnected elements. * Requires sharing of raw and processed data used in the study. * Reproducible workflows integrate various tools and practices to ensure consistency. * Uses tools like Docker to create isolated and reproducible computing environments. * Utilizes tools like Snakemake or Luigi to create reproducible data pipelines. ## Tools for reproducibility. * Various tools support reproducible research in statistical data science. * Integrate different aspects of the research workflow to enhance reproducibility. * Implementing best practices enhances the reproducibility of statistical data science projects. * Ensures transparency in the data preparation process for reproducibility. ## Challenges in reproducibility. * Various challenges can hinder the implementation of reproducible practices in data science. * Implements data management plans to ensure long-term viability of research data. * Emphasizes the importance of sharing raw data and analysis code in publications. * Utilizes open science frameworks for sharing anonymized data and analysis scripts. * Focuses on reproducibility in experimental setups and data analysis pipelines. * Evaluating the reproducibility of research is crucial for maintaining scientific integrity. * Implements various methods to assess and promote reproducible practices in data science. * Includes items related to data availability, code sharing, and documentation. * Helps standardize reproducibility practices across different research projects. * Involves attempting to reproduce key findings using provided data and code. * Implements recognition systems for studies meeting specific reproducibility criteria. * Encourages researchers to prioritize reproducible practices in their work. * The landscape of reproducibility in statistical data science continues to evolve. * Explores the use of AI techniques to enhance reproducibility in data science. * Implements automated code review systems to identify potential reproducibility issues. ### Reproducibility in big data era. * Implements distributed computing solutions for reproducible big data processing.

results.title: Data Use, Software, and Analysis Release Policies – ENCODE
results.content: # Data Use, Software, and Analysis Release Policies. ### Software and Analysis Release Policy for ENCODE Consortium Members. The ENCODE Project aims to enhance biomedical research by generating community resources of genomics data, software, tools and methods for genomics data analysis, and products resulting from data analyses and interpretations. As outlined in the ENCODE FOAs, NHGRI expects that the major resources resulting from this project, including data, software, and analyses, generated by the ENCODE awards will be made freely available to the research community. Timely release of software and analyses is a central part of ENCODE’s mission, to help to maximize the value of our work in the broader community, and enhance the reproducibility of our research. Thus we strongly encourage ENCODE-funded labs to provide useable, documented software and associated publications, for the mutual benefit of the publishing labs and the consortium. This document outlines policy for software and analysis release for ENCODE-funded research by all members of the ENCODE Consortium. ENCODE ***strongly encourages*** release of software tools and pipelines used for major analyses in planned ENCODE publications, and other software likely to be useful to multiple groups either within ENCODE or in the broader community. * ***How to release software:*** Software should be released by version controlled public repositories (e.g Github). * ***Accompanying publications:*** In addition to the release of well-documented code, we strongly encourage developers to publish citable descriptions of their software. We encourage (1) documenting these components; (2) providing scripts that reproduce key figures in ENCODE publications; (3) establishing reusable, publicly accessible analysis pipelines (e.g. Galaxy, virtual machines, Docker, DNA Nexus sessions); and (4) linking these through the DCC website. * ***Current and Future Support for Released Software:*** Software that will be released for publication and to repositories (e.g., Github) should state the types and degree of support users can expect for them to download, run and troubleshoot the available software as well as whether or not updates and “fixes” should be expected. Analyses comprising major ENCODE deliverables (e.g. the Encyclopedia) may be subject to pre-release vetting by consortium members.
